title: arXiv biology and biomedicine — week of 31 Oct–6 Nov 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending or readership chart. This is a relevance-ranked selection using sparse external discussion and other checkable signals, not a measured popularity ranking. arXiv incompletely covers biomedical research; many experimental and clinical preprints appear elsewhere.

sections.title: Headline
sections.text: Eight notable papers in the week of 31 October–6 November 2026 center on DNA design benchmarks, computational antibody and protein methods, and single-cell or cancer-genomics analyses. There is no defensible readership leaderboard: arXiv has no official trending chart, citations are absent or zero for the queried recent papers, and biomedical coverage is incomplete. The report focuses on what the studies tested and where biological or experimental validation remains limited. Snapshot 2026-11-06 02:21 UTC.

sections.title: BEND 2.0: Benchmarking the Capabilities Needed to Design DNA
sections.abstract: BEND 2.0 evaluates whether genomic models can predict the effects of DNA edits and use those predictions to guide sequence design.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors test eight tasks across five experimental datasets and report that frozen-representation linear readouts can match or beat native model outputs, while average-effect prediction can conceal weaker context-specific and mutation-interaction performance.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a benchmark on existing datasets, not prospective wet-lab confirmation of designed sequences; the authors note substantial room to improve context-specific and multi-cell design.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Covered by two independent research-news roundups; authors link a public leaderboard and code. Semantic Scholar returned 0 citations and 0 influential citations at snapshot, so this is limited attention evidence, not demonstrated adoption.

sections.title: iGC: Antibody Optimization via Reinforcement Learning over a Learned Somatic Hypermutation Prior
sections.abstract: iGC combines a learned somatic-hypermutation prior with reinforcement learning to optimize antigen-specific antibody sequences while constraining mutation patterns.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that the mutation prior more than doubles the strongest baseline on mutation-site prediction, and that optimized sequences retain somatic-hypermutation-like sequence structure while balancing reward and diversity.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper reports computational evaluation on existing repertoire, animal, and deep-mutational-scanning datasets; it describes no new animal experiments or prospective wet-lab validation of generated antibodies. Binding optimization is not evidence of therapeutic efficacy.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Discussed in two independent research-news roundups; Semantic Scholar returned 0 citations and 0 influential citations. The authors also report comparisons against mutation-prediction baselines.

sections.title: PeptSol: A Translational Benchmark for Protected-Peptide Solubility in Drug Manufacturing
sections.abstract: PeptSol provides a chemistry-aware benchmark for predicting solubility of protected peptide intermediates used in liquid-phase peptide synthesis.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors curate 1,388 measurements across 84 parent sequences and 101 protected structures. Across seven frozen encoders, the best reported macro-F1 is 0.843 for binary solubility and 0.614 for the harder three-class task in the stated historical-subset split.
sections.unique_caveat: 92.5% of measurements come from one historical programme. The authors report no consistent foundation-model advantage over explicit chemical fingerprints and descriptors; external chemistry and synthesis programmes are needed to test transfer.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv comment reports acceptance at the AI for Drug Discovery workshop, NeurIPS 2026; it also drew external research-summary coverage. Semantic Scholar returned 0 citations and 0 influential citations. Version 2 is a substantive update in this window.

sections.title: Evolutionary characterization of whole-genome doubling across human cancers
sections.abstract: The authors examine genomic and multi-omic patterns associated with whole-genome doubling across 41,332 tumours from 12 cancer types.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that driver mutations and homologous-recombination-deficiency mutagenesis generally precede doubling when both occur, and that post-doubling chromosome-arm losses vary less by cancer type. They also report reduced interferon-response and HLA-presentation programmes associated with epigenetic remodelling.
sections.unique_caveat: These are retrospective tumour-genomics associations, not causal tests of immune suppression or treatment response. Functional follow-up is needed before interpreting the proposed mechanisms.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in genomics and populations/evolution and surfaced in an independent genomics-paper index; Semantic Scholar returned 0 citations and 0 influential citations. Ranking reflects scope fit and dataset scale, not a measured attention lead.

sections.title: An auditable agentic pipeline for variant-to-gene prioritisation, validated against orthogonal functional evidence
sections.abstract: V2G records evidence retrieval and ranks candidate genes at GWAS loci; the authors test whether language-model reranking adds information beyond candidate ordering and prior knowledge.
sections.claimed_contribution: On 135 eligible held-out loci, the authors report Precision@1 of 0.793 versus 0.711 for the evidence ordering, but no detected difference from Open Targets L2G or training-membership baselines. Their ablations suggest the apparent gain largely reflects recall of known genes and anchoring to candidate order.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors report train/test overlap and note that the split does not fully separate associations. Performance on a constrained benchmark is not proof that retrieved molecular evidence caused better gene prioritisation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Covered in an independent genomics-paper index; Semantic Scholar returned 0 citations and 0 influential citations. Explicit ablations make the evidence boundary unusually checkable.

sections.title: Predicting protein structures at any folding stage from sequence
sections.abstract: FoldScape generates protein conformational ensembles conditioned on folding progress, rather than predicting only a native-state structure.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors train on about one million conformations from 10,000 sequences and report broader ensemble coverage than seed-varied AlphaFold 3 samples across three structural measures, while maintaining reconstruction accuracy over evaluated folding stages.
sections.unique_caveat: Broad coverage against generated AlphaFold ensembles is not validation against experimentally measured folding kinetics or equilibrium ensembles. Training combines simulated folding and mechanical-unfolding trajectories; authors say code and benchmark data are to be released on publication.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Independently indexed or summarized by Emergent Mind, Fugu-MT, and Papers.cool; Semantic Scholar returned 0 citations and 0 influential citations. Version 2 falls within the window.

sections.title: CellCanon: An Agentic Cellular World Model for Prediction, Explanation, and Observation-Driven Updating
sections.abstract: CellCanon combines single-cell expression prediction, evidence-grounded explanations, and updating from newly supplied observations.
sections.claimed_contribution: On 339 held-out SciPlex3 conditions across three cell lines, the authors report improvements in differential-expression AUPRC and Macro-F1 over the best baseline, plus an observation-update simulation that does not change model weights.
sections.unique_caveat: These are held-out benchmark and simulated-feedback results, not prospective experimental confirmation of predicted drug responses. A small set of cell lines and benchmark conditions does not establish transfer to other systems.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Received an external research-summary feature; Semantic Scholar did not return a record in the batch lookup, so no citation signal is available. It is directly relevant to single-cell response modelling.

sections.title: Coupling cellular trajectories and RNA kinetics on continuous expression manifolds with ManifoldVelo
sections.abstract: ManifoldVelo jointly estimates cell pseudotime and RNA-velocity dynamics using topology-conditioned continuous expression trajectories.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved pseudotime recovery in cyclic and branching simulations and directional agreement in velocity estimates, with real-data analyses consistent with differentiation stages and plate-held-out phase prediction.
sections.unique_caveat: RNA velocity and pseudotime are model-derived from transcriptomic snapshots, not direct observation of each cell's lineage. Real-data consistency is not independent lineage-tracing validation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors provide numerical source tables and code; Semantic Scholar returned 0 citations and 0 influential citations. No independent technical discussion was located in the sampled search, so it ranks on direct RNA/single-cell relevance rather than demonstrated attention.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.text: Three recurring method clusters appear in this selection, not a field-wide shift: DNA and antibody sequence models are evaluated as design tools (BEND 2.0, iGC); molecular modelling addresses manufacturing solubility and conformational ensembles (PeptSol, FoldScape); single-cell methods infer RNA dynamics or perturbation response (ManifoldVelo, CellCanon). WGD and V2G contribute genome-interpretation methods. These are computational and retrospective findings with uneven experimental validation.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.text: Author-stated limits include context-sensitive DNA design (BEND 2.0), concentrated source data (PeptSol), and incomplete association-level separation (V2G). Concrete follow-ups include blinded prospective assays for BEND 2.0 and iGC candidates; broader, programme- and scaffold-held-out PeptSol measurements; association-separated and retrieval-controlled V2G comparisons; experimental folding-ensemble checks for FoldScape; independent perturbation and lineage-tracing tests for CellCanon and ManifoldVelo; and longitudinal or perturbation-controlled studies of WGD-associated immune expression. These are synthesis proposals, not claims of novelty or clinical utility.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: The clearest common thread is evaluation: papers test what biological models can predict, design, or explain while exposing limits in transfer, context sensitivity, causal interpretation, or experimental confirmation. This is a relevance-ranked snapshot, not a popularity chart, and none of the reported computational results establishes clinical readiness.
